_comment: Transcription engine catalog. DATA, not code — replace this file without
a release, exactly as llm/models.json is replaced. Same reasoning: every
identifier and every price in this file changed within a month of being
written, and a catalog compiled into the code is wrong on the day it ships.
'languages' is the list the vendor publishes as supported. It is the whole
routing decision, so it is data too — a vendor adding Hebrew should be a
one-line edit and a re-run, not a code change.
'*' means the vendor claims general coverage and the router will use the
engine for any language, including an unspecified one.
Billing differs in kind between vendors and both shapes are here:
usd_per_hour        flat, by audio duration (xAI)
audio_in / text_out USD per million tokens (Google), with
usd_per_hour_est    the vendor's own blended estimate, used ONLY when a
response carries no usage counts. A cost derived
from it is marked estimated and never reads as
measured — see c1-first-cost-numbers.md for what
happens when those two are allowed to blur.
'max_seconds' is the duration limit WITH word timestamps and diarization
on, which is the only configuration this system uses. Google's own limit
is an hour without them and half that with them; the smaller number is the
real one here. Longer material is split — see asr/chunking.py.

_note: $0.10/hour batch, $0.20/hour streaming. Batch only here: a rough cut
is not a live product and streaming costs double for latency nobody
in this pipeline is waiting on.
The docs say 24 languages and then list 25 names; the list above is
the names, as codes. Hebrew is in neither count.
xAI's docs claim the model transcribes any language and that the
`language` field only gates text formatting. That would make Hebrew
3x cheaper here. It is unvalidated, so this list — not that claim —
is what routes. MISHNE_ASR_XAI_ANY_LANGUAGE=1 lifts the restriction
for a deliberate measurement run against Gemini output.
85+ languages including he-IL, which is why Hebrew lands here.
Word timestamps and diarization are file-mode only and cap a request
at 30 minutes; Google's own docs warn timestamps cost some accuracy.
Both are non-negotiable for this pipeline (asr/base.py), so the cap
applies to every request we make.
